sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球知名的大学，致力于解决当今世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境领域最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内合作创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学旨在提升所有生物生活质量的使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 请访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: These developments are run by the St. Louis Housing Authority.
sentences.zh: 这些开发项目由圣路易斯住房管理局运营。

sentences.en: This is a far cry from the crowded, collapsing tenements that many of these people have known.
sentences.zh: 这与许多这些人曾经住过的拥挤、倒塌的公寓楼形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Here in bright new buildings with spacious grounds, they can live.
sentences.zh: 在这里，在拥有宽敞场地的明亮新建筑里，他们能够生活。

sentences.en: The Pruitt-Igoe myth begins here.
sentences.zh: 普鲁伊特-戈伊的神话从这里开始。

sentences.en: They can live.
sentences.zh: 他们能够生活。

sentences.en: This is Chad Fredericks.
sentences.zh: 我是查德·弗雷德里克斯。

sentences.en: So Pruitt-Igoe was a public housing project that existed on the north side of St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 所以普鲁伊特-戈伊是一个曾存在于圣路易斯北部的公共住房项目。

sentences.en: Chad Fredericks is the director and producer of the documentary The Pruitt-Igoe Myth.
sentences.zh: 查德·弗雷德里克斯是纪录片《普鲁伊特-戈伊的神话》的导演兼制片人。

sentences.en: It was 33 11-story buildings, and it was part of a larger urban renewal campaign that the city was undergoing in the 1940s and 50s.
sentences.zh: 它由33栋11层的建筑组成，是该市在20世纪40和50年代进行的更大规模城市更新运动的一部分。

sentences.en: It was touted as a solution, a cure for the disease.
sentences.zh: 它被吹捧为一种解决方案，一种治愈这种疾病的良药。

sentences.en: It was viewed kind of as a replacement for low-rise tenement housing.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上被视为低层公寓住宅的替代品。

sentences.en: People who had been living where they literally never saw the sun.
sentences.zh: 那些以前生活在 literalmente 见不到阳光的地方的人们。

sentences.en: And so Pruitt-Igoe was supposed to be everything different.
sentences.zh: 因此，普鲁伊特-戈伊本应带来截然不同的体验。

sentences.en: Now they would have more magnificent views than the richest people in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们将拥有比圣路易斯最富有的人还要壮丽的视野。

sentences.en: It was high-rise, whereas the private market housing was low-rise.
sentences.zh: 它是高层的，而私营市场的住房则是低层的。

sentences.en: It was federal, and therefore you wouldn't have the creeping influence of slumlords coming in and basically being derelict landowners.
sentences.zh: 它是联邦性质的，因此你不会遭遇那种偷偷摸摸的、形同失职地主的无良房东的侵蚀影响。

sentences.en: It was an opportunity to present poor residents with light and air.
sentences.zh: 这是一个为贫困居民提供光线和空气的机会。

sentences.en: That was really the driving factor behind Pruitt-Igoe's design.
sentences.zh: 这确实是普鲁伊特-戈伊设计背后的驱动因素。

sentences.en: Tall, modern buildings would give access to fresh breezes and sunlight,
sentences.zh: 高大、现代的建筑将带来新鲜微风和阳光，

sentences.en: the sensible remedy to the unhealthy conditions in the inner-city sluMs.
sentences.zh: 这是对内城贫民窟不健康状况的明智补救措施。

sentences.en: At least that was the thinking.
sentences.zh: 至少当时的设想是这样的。

sentences.en: Pruitt-Igoe would rise above the polluted sluMs.
sentences.zh: 普鲁伊特-戈伊将凌驾于污染严重的贫民窟之上。

sentences.en: It was a very beautiful place, like a big hotel resort, I'd say,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常美丽的地方，就像一个大型度假村，我想说，

sentences.en: with plenty of green grass, trees, shrubbery, and all the works.
sentences.zh: 有着充足的绿草、树木、灌木和各种配套设施。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, one day we woke up and it was all gone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一天我们醒来，这一切都不复存在了。

sentences.en: In the middle 50s, St. Louis thought it had solved its low-cost housing needs,
sentences.zh: 在50年代中期，圣路易斯认为它已经解决了低成本住房的需求，

sentences.en: but instead a monster was created.
sentences.zh: 但相反，却创造出了一个怪物。

sentences.en: In the film The Pruitt-Igoe Myth, it's made very clear that the project wasn't just a monster.
sentences.zh: 在电影《普鲁伊特-戈伊的神话》中，人们非常清楚地表明，这个项目不仅仅是一个怪物。

sentences.en: In the beginning especially.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在一开始的时候。

sentences.en: It represented hope to thousands of people who never thought they'd live in a clean, new home.
sentences.zh: 它给成千上万从未想过能住进干净新家的穷苦人们带来了希望。

sentences.en: But things went downhill very faSt.
sentences.zh: 但事情急转直下。

sentences.en: 12,000 people were originally jammed into these 33 buildings.
sentences.zh: 最初有12,000人被挤在这33栋建筑里。

sentences.en: Only 2,500 people still linger in the remaining shelves.
sentences.zh: 如今只剩下2,500人还在残存的建筑中徘徊。

sentences.en: Maintenance dropped off.
sentences.zh: 维护工作开始松懈。

sentences.en: Elevators and trash incinerators broke and remained broken.
sentences.zh: 电梯和垃圾焚化炉坏了之后就再也没有修好。

sentences.en: Vandalism and crime rates rose.
sentences.zh: 破坏公物和犯罪率上升了。

sentences.en: The one thing you always ask yourself is, why?
sentences.zh: 你总是会问自己的一个问题是，为什么？

sentences.en: Why is it like this?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why do I live here?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要住在这里？

sentences.en: What did I do wrong?
sentences.zh: 我做错了什么？

sentences.en: I think it created a mindset for the inhabitants that they weren't cared about.
sentences.zh: 我认为这给居民们造成了一种心态，即他们是不被关心的。

sentences.en: And I think that manifested itself in a way that calls more harm to the tenants than any other entity.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种心态的表现方式，对租户造成的伤害比任何其他实体都要大。

sentences.en: The vandalism that existed in Pruitt-Igoe came from that environment.
sentences.zh: 普鲁伊特-戈伊存在的破坏行为正是源于那种环境。

sentences.en: Things allowed to just deteriorate and people not really care.
sentences.zh: 任由事物恶化，而人们并不真正在乎。

sentences.en: It's easy to look at Pruitt-Igoe and think that almost every decision that was made was a bad one.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易看着普鲁伊特-戈伊，然后认为几乎每一个做出的决定都是糟糕的。

sentences.en: The vandalism led the Housing Authority to install a bunch of unbreakable designs in the towers.
sentences.zh: 破坏行为促使住房管理局在这些高楼里安装了一堆无法破坏的设计。

sentences.en: Instead of trying to enhance their existence, we'll just make things so they can't be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 与其试图提升他们的生活状况，不如让我们把东西做得无法摧毁。

sentences.en: Everything had to be protected.
sentences.zh: 一切都必须受到保护。

sentences.en: Light fixtures, no light exposed.
sentences.zh: 灯具，不暴露任何光线。

sentences.en: There were shields around them with mesh metal protecting the bulb.
sentences.zh: 它们周围有带有金属网的防护罩来保护灯泡。

sentences.en: The city made a big deal about this.
sentences.zh: 这座城市对此大肆宣传。

sentences.en: Their PR department actually came out and they had the installation of these new unbreakable lights that were going out.
sentences.zh: 他们的公关部门实际上走出来，展示了这些即将投入使用的全新防碎灯具的安装。

sentences.en: And, you know, they brought in all these people in the press.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们请来了所有这些媒体人员。

sentences.en: The only human reaction to being presented with an unbreakable object is to try and break it.
sentences.zh: 面对一个不可摧毁的物体，人类唯一的自然反应就是试图去摧毁它。

sentences.en: You know, the fact that it was indestructible made you want to try to destroy things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它是不可摧毁的事实反而让你想要试着去破坏东西。

sentences.en: There was a screen around the light bulbs that kept you from breaking them.
sentences.zh: 灯泡周围有一个网罩，可以防止你打破它们。

sentences.en: But, you know, kids will be kids.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，小孩子嘛总归是小孩子。

sentences.en: Find a way to break it.
sentences.zh: 总会找到打破它的办法。

sentences.en: And we just put water in it, throw it up.
sentences.zh: 我们就在里面装上水，然后把它扔上去。

sentences.en: And the light would get hot and it would break and the lights are out.
sentences.zh: 然后灯变热了，它就会碎掉，灯就灭了。

sentences.en: Two decades after opening Pruitt-Igoe, the government gave up.
sentences.zh: 在普鲁伊特-戈伊开放二十年后，政府放弃了。

sentences.en: Because they are so desperate, they are willing to try desperate things.
sentences.zh: 因为他们走投无路，所以愿意尝试绝望的手段。

sentences.en: The housing authority blew it up.
sentences.zh: 住房管理局把它炸毁了。

sentences.en: The press was invited.
sentences.zh: 媒体受到了邀请。

sentences.en: It started with three buildings in 1972.
sentences.zh: 它始于1972年的三栋建筑。

sentences.en: The rest followed.
sentences.zh: 其余的也相继被毁。

sentences.en: The image of the implosion with the St. Louis Gateway arch in the background became infamous.
sentences.zh: 伴随着圣路易斯大拱门作为背景的爆破场景的影像变得臭名昭著。

sentences.en: The Pruitt-Igoe myth begins here.
sentences.zh: 普鲁伊特-戈伊的神话从这里开始。

sentences.en: It was viewed as symbolic.
sentences.zh: 它被视为具有象征意义。

sentences.en: It was kind of viewed as an end of an era.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上被视为一个时代的终结。

sentences.en: So then several years later, Charles Jenks writes his book on postmodern architecture.
sentences.zh: 因此，几年后，查尔斯·詹克斯写了他关于后现代主义建筑的书。

sentences.en: And he opens his book with Pruitt-Igoe's implosion as the death of modern architecture.
sentences.zh: 他在书中以普鲁伊特-戈伊的爆破作为现代主义建筑死亡的开篇。

sentences.en: Which leads to this question.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了这样一个问题。

sentences.en: How well known would Pruitt-Igoe be if you didn't have that implosion image?
sentences.zh: 如果没有那个爆破影像，普鲁伊特-戈伊会有多知名？

sentences.en: You know, if it's not blown up and you don't have that image with the arch in the background and it's so poignant,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果没有被炸毁，也没有那个以拱门为背景且如此动人心魄的影像，

sentences.en: would we be discussing Pruitt-Igoe?
sentences.zh: 我们还会讨论普鲁伊特-戈伊吗？

sentences.en: And I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我想不会。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, something becomes an icon because it's been visually recorded.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，某个事物之所以成为偶像，是因为它被视觉记录了下来。

sentences.en: There's something about that building in freefall that acts as better evidence than anything else for failure.
sentences.zh: 自由落体中的那栋建筑，似乎比任何其他东西都更能作为失败的证据。

sentences.en: That image was so powerful, so full of emotion,
sentences.zh: 那个影像如此震撼，充满了情感，

sentences.en: that it could easily be used to support any previously held beliefs or prejudices about federal housing
sentences.zh: 以至于它可以轻易地被用来支持任何先前存在的关于联邦住房、

sentences.en: or modernist architecture or even the poor themselves.
sentences.zh: 现代主义建筑甚至穷人本身的信念或偏见。

sentences.en: And so people will use it constantly as such.
sentences.zh: 因此人们会不断地这样使用它。

sentences.en: That's what people think when they think of public housing,
sentences.zh: 这就是人们想到公共住房时的想法，

sentences.en: when they think of large-scale federal prograMs.
sentences.zh: 当他们想到大型联邦项目时。

sentences.en: It's just an architectural failure and here's a building that's being imploded because it was bad architecture.
sentences.zh: 它只是一次建筑上的失败，这里有一栋正在被爆破的建筑，因为它是不好的建筑。

sentences.en: Bad architecture is one of the major cited reasons for why Pruitt-Igoe failed.
sentences.zh: 拙劣的建筑被认为是普鲁伊特-戈伊失败的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: But that actually isn't a factor that Chad Fredericks puts a lot of stock in.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这并不是查尔斯·弗雷德里克斯看重的因素。

sentences.en: Architecture was a marginal influence, if any, on Pruitt-Igoe's demise.
sentences.zh: 建筑对普鲁伊特-戈伊的消亡充其量只是一个微不足道的影响。

sentences.en: Perhaps this is an overreaction, but I tend to look as far away as I can from the design of the building
sentences.zh: 也许这是一种过度反应，但我倾向于尽可能不去考虑建筑的设计，

sentences.en: simply because I see so many other compelling factors in Pruitt-Igoe's decline.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为我在普鲁伊特-戈伊的衰落中看到了许多其他更具说服力的因素。

sentences.en: I don't like to try to take Pruitt-Igoe out of the city in which it resides.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢把普鲁伊特-戈伊从它所在的城市中剥离出来看待。

sentences.en: And I think many of the discussions that people have about Pruitt-Igoe tend to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对普鲁伊特-戈伊的很多讨论往往都在这样做。

sentences.en: They tend to look at Pruitt-Igoe as something that's somehow divorced from the city of St. Louis
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于将普鲁伊特-戈伊视为某种与圣路易斯市脱节的事物，

sentences.en: and what it went through in those years.
sentences.zh: 仿佛它与这座城市在那些年里经历的一切无关。

sentences.en: What St. Louis went through was a completely unpredicted population decline.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯经历的是一场完全无法预测的人口下降。

sentences.en: You have to remember, Pruitt-Igoe comes out of the 1949 Housing Act.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，普鲁伊特-戈伊源于1949年的《住房法案》。

sentences.en: And in 1949, the population of most major cities in the urban core was rising.
sentences.zh: 而在1949年，大多数主要城市核心区的人口都在增长。

sentences.en: It was rising relatively rapidly, people coming into the cities for jobs from rural areas.
sentences.zh: 增长速度相对较快，人们从农村地区涌入城市寻找工作。

sentences.en: And so St. Louis was undergoing the same process where they just had crowds and crowds of people
sentences.zh: 因此，圣路易斯也经历了同样的过程，成群结队的人

sentences.en: coming into the city.
sentences.zh: 涌入这座城市。

sentences.en: And so the idea was, well, we need to find a place to put all of these new people
sentences.zh: 所以当时的设想是，我们需要找到一个地方来安置所有这些新来的人，

sentences.en: in a way that doesn't lead to the kinds of slums that you had in earlier years
sentences.zh: 且这种安置方式不会导致早期出现的那种贫民窟，

sentences.en: going all the way back to the 19th century factory city.
sentences.zh: 一直追溯到19世纪的工厂城市。

sentences.en: The understanding among city planners and city officials was that the population would continue
sentences.zh: 城市规划者和市政官员的共识是，从1950年到1970年，人口将继续

sentences.en: to rise to a population of about a million from 800,000 from 1950 to 1970.
sentences.zh: 从80万增长到大约100万。

sentences.en: And so over the course of those 20 years, there was an expectation that the city would rise
sentences.zh: 因此，在这20年的时间里，人们期望这座城市的人口会

sentences.en: maybe 20% in terms of its population.
sentences.zh: 增长大约20%。

sentences.en: What happened was the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 但实际发生的情况却完全相反。

sentences.en: The bottom dropped out of the city's population as populations started to move to suburban areas
sentences.zh: 随着人口开始向市郊迁移，城市人口急剧跌入谷底，

sentences.en: out of the city.
sentences.zh: 离开了这座城市。

sentences.en: And this process was aided by the exact same 1949 Federal Housing Act that offered federally
sentences.zh: 这一过程得到了完全相同的1949年《联邦住房法案》的推波助澜，该法案为在郊区买房提供了联邦担保贷款。

sentences.en: underwritten loans to buy houses in suburbia.
sentences.zh: 你真的开始看到人口骤降。

sentences.en: You really started to see populations dip.
sentences.zh: 普鲁伊特-戈伊被创造它的那部法律所削弱。

sentences.en: Pruitt-Igoe was undercut by the very law that created it.
sentences.zh: 以至于到了1980年，圣路易斯的人口只有1950年的一半。

sentences.en: To the point where by 1980, St. Louis had half the population that it did in 1950.
sentences.zh: 这种趋势一直延续到今天。

sentences.en: And that trend continues to this day.
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，你建造了这个庞大的项目来安置所有涌入城市的人。

sentences.en: What happens is you build this massive project to house all these people who are coming into
sentences.zh: 而当这些人没有来，而你原本打算住在那里的人却搬走了，

sentences.en: the city.
sentences.zh: 你突然间就面临着空置危机。

sentences.en: And when those people don't come and the people who you intended to be living there move out,
sentences.zh: 这确实是困扰圣路易斯这些年的问题。

sentences.en: all of a sudden you have a vacancy crisis.
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于此，查德将普鲁伊特-戈伊的消亡归咎于主要的建筑或设计缺陷，

sentences.en: And that's really what gripped St. Louis during these years.
sentences.zh: 其实是该项目的庞大规模。

sentences.en: So given that, the major architectural or design flaw that Chad attributes to the demise of Pruitt-Igoe
sentences.zh: 它建得太大了，到20世纪70年代，根本没有足够的人口来填满它。

sentences.en: was the sheer scale of the project.
sentences.zh: 所以这才是普鲁伊特-戈伊真正的悲剧所在，但这也是一件非常难以预测的事情。

sentences.en: It was built so big and there just simply weren't enough people to populate it by the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 规模从一开始就注定了普鲁伊特-戈伊的命运。

sentences.en: And so that's the real tragedy of Pruitt-Igoe, but it's something that was very difficult
sentences.zh: 高空置率意味着住房管理局无法收到足够的资金

sentences.en: to predict as well.
sentences.zh: 来支付维护账单。

sentences.en: The scale doomed Pruitt-Igoe from the start.
sentences.zh: 运营和维护建筑物的资金本应来自租户的租金收入。

sentences.en: The high vacancy rate meant that the house and authority couldn't collect enough money
sentences.zh: 事情开始损坏。

sentences.en: to pay the maintenance bills.
sentences.zh: 状况恶化了。

sentences.en: The money for operating and maintaining the buildings was to come from the incomes
sentences.zh: 更多的人离开了。

sentences.en: of the rents from the tenants.
sentences.zh: 能收到的租金变少了。

sentences.en: Things began to break.
sentences.zh: 一切都变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: Conditions deteriorated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我经常喜欢说，普鲁伊特-戈伊是一个容易成为替罪羊的对象。

sentences.en: More people left.
sentences.zh: 它是高层建筑。
